units.thermal_conductivity_k: Btu·in/(hr·ft²·°F) at the stated mean temperature

conventions.unverified: The literal string 'unverified' means the value was not found in a published source. Nothing was guessed, averaged, or converted from SI to fill a gap. Where only SI values exist they are quoted as printed in a note and the inch-pound field stays 'unverified'.
conventions.src: Every fact carries 'src', a list of ids in that material's own 'sources' array. Each source has its exact URL, publication number or date, access date and retrieval method.
conventions.products: Values are per product and never merged. Where two products differ, both are given and the difference is listed in 'discrepancies_between_products'.
conventions.typical_values: Manufacturer data sheets report typical or average values subject to manufacturing variation and change without notice. Confirm against the current sheet before using a number in a submittal.

method: Manufacturer PDFs were downloaded and read from their raw text (pdftotext). Where a table was an image, the rendered page was read instead; this is noted on that source's 'retrieval'. ASTM scope text comes from the public astm.org store pages, since full ASTM tables are paywalled.
product_availability_notes: Fiberglass: Owens Corning's current factory ASJ/SSL product is 'SSL II with ASJ Max Fiberglas Pipe Insulation' (Pub. 20547), which is the product recorded.
Mineral wool: the current MinWool-1200 Pipe sheet is Johns Manville-branded. Earlier sheets (2019) and JM doc IND-505 say Industrial Insulation Group, LLC (IIG) manufactures MinWool-1200.

Calcium silicate: JM Thermo-1200 replaced IIG/JM Thermo-12 Gold starting in 2017. JM FAQ IND-305 says 'Once we make the conversion at our manufacturing facilities, we will produce only Thermo-1200.' Thermo-12 Gold data comes from its last sheet (IND-300 12-16, © Industrial Insulation Group, LLC).

Cellular glass: no product named 'FOAMGLAS 18' was found in the foamglas.com catalog or the Owens Corning product guide (April 2026); '18' appears to refer to the 18 in. block width. Only FOAMGLAS ONE is populated.

Elastomeric: K-FLEX ST is an EU product, not in the K-FLEX USA catalog, and is published in SI only, so its inch-pound fields are 'unverified'. K-FLEX Insul-Tube (the uncoated core of TITAN, C534 Type 1 Grade 1) was added as K-FLEX USA's direct equivalent to AP ArmaFlex.

Phenolic: Kingspan's US Technical Insulation page lists no Kooltherm pipe product (only Tarec polyiso pipe products), and no US Kooltherm pipe data sheet was found. The EU sheet's SI values are quoted in notes only. Resolco Insul-Phen is the populated phenolic product.

astm_spec.designation: ASTM C547-25 (active edition per ASTM store page; prior editions include C547-22a, C547-22, C547-19, C547-17)
astm_spec.title: Standard Specification for Mineral Fiber Pipe Insulation
astm_spec.scope_summary: 1.1 Covers mineral fiber insulation produced to form hollow cylinders for standard pipe and tubing sizes, molded or precision v-grooved, with one or more walls split longitudinally, for use on pipe temperatures up to 1400°F (760°C). 1.2 Sub-ambient applications need properly installed protective vapor retarders or barriers (refers to Practice C921). 1.3 Flexible mineral fiber wraps (perpendicular-oriented fiber rolls, non-precision or manually scored block/board, flexible boards or blankets used as pipe insulation) are NOT covered. Abstract: materials are classified into five types (by processing method and operating temperature) and two grades (by heating requirements); fiber may be rock, slag, or glass.

types_grades.note: Both fiberglass products cite ASTM C547 Type I. OC: 'meets the performance requirements of ASTM C547 Type I with a maximum temperature of 850°F (454°C)'. JM: 'ASTM C547 Type I (Replaces HH-I-558B, Form D, Type III, Class 12, Class 13 up to 850°F [454°C])'. The full five-type temperature table of C547-25 is behind the ASTM paywall and is not reproduced on the public scope page.
OC: 'Rated per ASTM C547, Type I, Grade A — Pipe insulation can be installed on in-service/hot pipes with an operating temperature up to 850°F (454°C).' JM data sheet does not state a grade.

astm_spec.title: Standard Specification for Calcium Silicate Block and Pipe Thermal Insulation
astm_spec.scope_summary: Scope 1.1: 'covers calcium silicate block and pipe thermal insulation for use on surfaces with temperatures between 80 and 1700°F (27 to 927°C), unless otherwise agreed upon between the manufacturer and the purchaser.' Abstract: three types (Type I, Type IA, Type II); material is 'principally of hydrous calcium silicate usually with the incorporation of fibrous reinforcement'. Tests cover thermal conductivity, linear shrinkage after heat soaking, flexural strength, compressive strength, mass loss by tumbling, hot surface performance, surface burning, stress corrosion, and moisture content.

types_grades.note: NIA: Type I max k 0.41 Btu·in/(hr·ft²·°F) at 100°F mean. Both Type I products here are rated 1200°F by their manufacturers. JM guide spec: 'Type 1 Maximum density of 15 lbs/ft3'.
NIA: Types IA and II max k 0.50 at 100°F mean. JM guide spec: 'Type 1A Maximum density of 20 lbs/ft3'.
JM's ASTM C533 Type II product (Super Caltemp Gold 1700 block) has a 1700°F operating limit, matching the top of the C533 scope. NIA: max k 0.50 at 100°F mean.

astm_spec.other: NIA: the types are 'classified primarily by maximum-use temperature and density'; the standard also covers flexural and compressive strength, linear shrinkage, surface burning, and maximum moisture content as shipped.

spec_limits_per_nia_chart.note: Secondary source. NIA: 'This chart provides the reader with material properties as typically specified in ASTM material specifications ... All properties should be verified with individual manufacturers'; 'Some values such as specific thermal conductivities at various mean temperatures may be interpolated or extrapolated by a small amount'. N/A = mean temperature outside the standard's scope; N/S = not stated in the standard; N/R = not required for this classification. These are spec limits (max k, min strength), not product values.

astm_spec.title: Standard Specification for Cellular Glass Thermal Insulation
astm_spec.scope_summary: Covers composition, sizes, dimensions and physical properties of cellular glass thermal insulation for commercial or industrial systems operating between −450 and 800°F (−268 and 427°C). Special fabrication or techniques for pipe insulation may be required from 250 to 800°F (121 to 427°C); contact the manufacturer. Actual temperature limits for specific applications are agreed between manufacturer and purchaser. Does not cover building-envelope cellular glass (see C1902). Scope 1.3: 'Cellular glass insulation has the potential to exhibit stress cracks if the rate of temperature change exceeds 200°F (112°C) per hour.' Pipe/tubing fabrication from block is governed by ASTM C1639 (current: C1639-19(2025)), which requires all materials to meet C552, limits sectional pipe insulation to not more than four through joints per full section (excluding the half-section mating plane), and specifies fabrication adhesives (hot asphalt for below-ambient; hot asphalt, elastomeric asphalt or gypsum-based cement for above-ambient).

types_grades.note: C552 scope upper limit is 800°F for all cellular glass covered by the spec. OC states FOAMGLAS ONE is 'Type 1 Block (Grade 6)'. Types II–IV are fabricated shapes made by fabricators from Type I block (NIA Insulation Outlook, 2012). The current C552-22 type/grade table itself is behind the ASTM paywall and was not viewed.
OC product guide: FOAMGLAS HLB 800/1000/1200/1400/1600/2400 = ASTM C552 Grade 8/10/12/14/16/24 (tank bases, load-bearing pipe supports).

types_grades.type: C552 maximum k for Type 1 Block, Grade 6 (as reproduced by OC)
types_grades.note: Limit values reproduced in the OC FOAMGLAS ONE data sheet ('Type 1 Block (Grade 6) limit values ... specified by ASTM C552'); −265°F listed as N/A.

spec_limits_per_nia_chart.cross_check: The Type I block k limits match the C552 Grade 6 maximums reprinted on the FOAMGLAS ONE data sheet (0.21 at -100°F, 0.27 at 0°F, 0.31 at 75°F, 0.40 at 200°F, 0.58 at 400°F). Type II (pipe) limits are higher, consistent with the EU sheet's note that fabricated pipe sections have a higher λ than block.
spec_limits_per_nia_chart.note: Secondary source. NIA: 'This chart provides the reader with material properties as typically specified in ASTM material specifications ... All properties should be verified with individual manufacturers'; 'Some values such as specific thermal conductivities at various mean temperatures may be interpolated or extrapolated by a small amount'. N/A = mean temperature outside the standard's scope; N/S = not stated in the standard; N/R = not required for this classification. These are spec limits (max k, min strength), not product values.

astm_spec.scope_summary: 1.1: Covers faced or unfaced rigid cellular phenolic thermal insulation. Boards shall be faced or unfaced. Tubular forms and board cut from a block or bun shall be unfaced (Note 1: if a facer or vapor retarder is used on the tubular form, refer to Practice C921). Does not apply to field-expanded cellular phenolic. 1.2: Used as roof insulation; sheathing/rigid board for non-load-bearing building applications; and pipe or board insulation cut from a block or bun for use between -40 and 257°F (-40 and 125°C). Type II and Type III materials with an appropriate vapor retarder covering on the warm surface are used to a lower temperature limit of -290°F (-180°C). 1.4: Covers closed-cell material made with blowing agents of ozone depletion potential 0. Abstract lists required properties: density, compressive resistance, tensile strength, apparent thermal conductivity, dimensional stability, water absorption, water vapor permeance and permeability, flame spread index, smoke developed index (the numeric limits are in the paywalled standard and are not reproduced here).

discrepancies_between_products: Service temperature: Resolco -290°F to 250°F vs Kingspan EU sheet -50°C to +110°C (SI as published). Kingspan's range is far narrower at both ends.
ASTM C1126 classification: Resolco claims Type II and III, Grade 1 (printed 'type 11 and 111'); Kingspan EU sheet claims Type III - Grade 1.
Closed cell content: Resolco minimum 92% (ASTM D6226) vs Kingspan EU >= 95% (EN ISO 4590).
Water absorption: Resolco 0.61 vol% (ASTM C209) vs Kingspan EU <= 3 vol% (ASTM C1126 & C209) - Kingspan figure is a limit-style value, Resolco a typical result.
Fire: Resolco publishes ASTM E84 25/50 up to 3 in; Kingspan EU sheet publishes only EN 13501-1 BL-s1,d0 and BS 476 Class O (no E84).
Units: Resolco publishes inch-pound only; Kingspan EU publishes SI only (no IP values recorded).
Resolco internal: compressive strength 24.1 psi at 10% deflection (data sheet, Jan 2018) vs 'Compressive Strength 29lb/in2' minimum property (install guide spec 5.3.1.2, 2018).

Resolco internal: quick spec says 'Coating the pipe for rust prevention is not required', while the install guide spec (4.2.3) calls for two coats of epoxy on carbon steel below 25°F and stainless steel between 25°F and 250°F.
Resolco internal: install guide references ASTM C-1126-00; data sheet references the 2017 revision; current edition is C1126-24.
Resolco internal: vapor stops at 21 ft intervals (quick spec) vs where straight runs exceed 24 ft (install guide 6.1.1.12.1).
unverified: products[Resolco].thermal_conductivity.points - only one k value (0.180) published, mean temperature not stated; no k-vs-mean-temperature curve found
products[Resolco].water_vapor.material_permeability - perm-in value not published
products[Resolco].sizes.iron_pipe_nps / copper_tube / thickness_in / section_length_in - no stock size table; fabricated to order by approved fabricators
products[Resolco].combustibility - no ASTM E136 statement either way
products[Kingspan] - no US Kooltherm Pipe Insulation data sheet exists on Kingspan US site; all inch-pound fields unverified; EU SI values recorded in notes only
products[Kingspan].thermal_conductivity curve - EU sheet refers to the DoP for λ(T); DoP not retrieved

Exact ASTM C1126-24 Type III Grade 1 numeric requirements are in the paywalled standard. Spec-level limits are now recorded from the NIA chart (secondary) under astm_spec.spec_limits_per_nia_chart: 257°F max, -290°F min, k max 0.18–0.24 at 75°F, compressive min 18 psi, WVP max 5.0 perm-in.
